First, we rewrite the polynomial, interpreting any constants as multiples of the identity matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(X) & ={X}^{2}-2X-3 \\  & ={X}^{2}-2X-3I\end{aligned}
$$

So, we want to find $f(A)={A}^{2}-2A-3I.$

Let's calculate ${A}^{2}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{2} & =A\cdot A \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 & -2 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}4 & -2 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}14 & -10 \\ 5 & -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can evaluate $f(A):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(A) & ={A}^{2}-2A-3I \\  & =[\begin{aligned}14 & -10 \\ 5 & -1\end{aligned}]-2[\begin{aligned}4 & -2 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]-3[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}14 & -10 \\ 5 & -1\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}8 & -4 \\ 2 & 2\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}14-8-3 & -10-(-4)-0 \\ 5-2-0 & -1-2-3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -6 \\ 3 & -6\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
